issues.detail: The two examples are prose descriptions of what an agent does rather than runnable end-to-end demonstrations, with only one-line inline snippets and no concrete output shown.

scenarios.name: add-column-migration-safely
scenarios.rationale: Both cover the generate/addColumn(TEXT, allowNull)/removeColumn/db:migrate/db:migrate:undo flow and warn against sync alter; B shows a fuller model update with a nullable type (string | null), while A's model snippet is minimal and A adds extra transaction/lock_timeout complexity without model typing.

scenarios.name: typescript-models-with-managed-transaction
scenarios.rationale: Both use declare fields, CreationOptional, hasMany/belongsTo with authorId, and a managed transaction passing the transaction to both creates; B is more complete with ForeignKey typing, association declarations, and explicit FK definitions, while A omits createdAt/updatedAt on Post and has less thorough association typing.

scenarios.name: eager-load-and-safe-raw-query
scenarios.rationale: Both responses cover every rubric item: include with where published:true and required:false, order createdAt DESC, limit 10, and sequelize.query with replacements and QueryTypes.SELECT with no interpolation; A adds the subquery/limit note and Postgres count-type caveat, while B adds separate:true and its raw query has a minor GROUP BY nuance, so A is marginally more thorough.
